overview: The file contains American Consul John Carter Vincent’s report on the Manchu-Japanese Economic Conference held at Dairen on August 15–17, 1933, together with a translated newspaper version of Lieutenant General Kuniaki Koiso’s principal address. Vincent portrays the gathering as a largely ceremonial exercise intended to impress Manchurian delegates and promote a Japan–Manchukuo economic bloc, noting that its closed committees apparently produced few concrete results, although Japanese commercial interests privately pressed for lower Manchukuo tariffs. Koiso’s speech presents the Kwantung Army’s economic vision for Manchukuo, including integrated transport, road and river development, cotton cultivation, colonization, mining, timber, heavy industry, and the abolition of extraterritoriality.
